newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks open firmer on land liquidity report.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks open firmer on land liquidity report.

text.p: Tokyo stocks opened slightly higher on Monday, as property-related shares were encouraged by a newspaper report that the government plans to allow in April the securitisation of collateralised land, aiming to boost liquidity in the nation's land market.
The 225-share Nikkei average gained 67.48 points or 0.36 percent to trade at 18,700.64 in the first 10 minutes of trade.
Its June futures rose 90 points to 18,680.
"Bank, real estate and construction shares are likely to lead the market today," said Kenji Karikomi, deputy general manager at Daiwa Securities Co Ltd.
Top percentage gainers on the Tokyo Stock Exchange's first section were fisheries, real estate, transportation equipment and banks.

The Japanese financial daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said on Monday the government will from April allow the securitisation of collateralised land used for commercial purposes as part of a set of measures to boost liquidity in the property market to be announced by the end of this month.
